title: The Four Status Flags: Zero, Sign, Carry and Overflow
unit: Design of the Arithmetic and Logic Unit
quickIdea: Every ALU operation leaves four status bits behind: Z says the result was zero, N repeats the result's top bit, C reports the carry out, and V reports that a signed result did not fit. C and V answer different questions and are never interchangeable.
remember: Z = 1 when every result bit is 0; N = the result's most significant bit, which is the sign only for signed values.
C is the carry out of the top bit: for an addition it means the unsigned result needed n+1 bits, and for A - B it means there was no borrow, so A >= B.
V = the exclusive-or of the carry into the sign column and the carry out of it; it means a signed result fell outside the n-bit two's complement range.
C and V can differ: adding 1111 and 0001 in 4 bits gives carry out 1 with no overflow, because -1 + 1 = 0 fits.
The flags are captured into a status register at the end of the cycle and are read by later conditional instructions; an instruction that does not write them leaves the old values in place.
In 4-bit addition, 64 of the 256 ordered operand pairs set V, and 64 of the 256 ordered subtraction pairs give the wrong answer from the raw sign bit.

example.prompt: A 4-bit ALU adds 0111 and 0001. Give the result and all four flags, and say which instruction would be misled by each.
example.work: 0111 + 0001 = 1000, with carry out 0. The result is 1000, whose top bit is 1, so N = 1 and Z = 0. The carry into the sign column was 1 (from adding 1+1 in bit 2) and the carry out was 0, so V = 1: signed, 7 + 1 = 8 does not fit in -8..7. C = 0, so an unsigned reading would think the sum fits, which it does - 7 + 1 = 8 fits in 0..15.
example.answer: Result 1000, Z = 0, N = 1, C = 0, V = 1: no unsigned carry, but a signed overflow.

gateAngle: Flag questions are decided by recomputing the two carries into and out of the top column. GATE CSE 2022 Q.8 (in the fixed-point card of the Digital Logic subject) asks exactly this for four candidate operand pairs; the same two-carry test also tells you when a comparison flag is trustworthy, which is the SLT card's correction.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: In 4-bit two's complement, subtract 0001 from 1000. Give Z, N, C and V and say what each means.
variations.answer: Z = 0, N = 0, C = 1, V = 0: unsigned, -8 seen as 8 is >= 1; signed, -8 - 1 = -9 does not fit, and the C = 1 answer is nonsense for signed values - which is why V exists.
variations.why: 1000 - 0001 = 1000 + 1110 + 1 = 1 0111. Kept result 0111: Z = 0, N = 0. Carry out 1, so C = 1 and, for a subtraction, there was no borrow, meaning -8 >= 1 is claimed. The carries into and out of the sign column are 1 and 1, so V = 0.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why does the carry flag not report signed overflow?
variations.answer: Because the carry out of the top bit only says the unsigned value needed an extra bit; a signed result can overflow with no carry out at all.
variations.why: The two questions have different answers on the same addition, so two bits are needed.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: Which flags does a logic operation such as AND normally affect, and which does it leave alone?
variations.answer: It sets Z and N from the result and leaves C and V alone, since a bitwise operation has no carry and no range.
variations.why: The flags a design chooses to write are part of the instruction set contract, and questions about stale flags depend on it.

trap.what: Treating C and V as the same bit under two names.
trap.why: C reports the unsigned range, V the signed range, and one addition can set one without the other.
trap.counterexample: 4-bit: 1111 + 0001 = 1 0000. Carry out 1, so C = 1; carries into and out of the sign column are both 1, so V = 0. Nothing overflowed in signed terms, because -1 + 1 = 0.

check.question: For 4-bit two's complement addition, how many of the 256 ordered operand pairs set V, and why is the count not symmetric?
check.answer: 64: 28 pairs of two non-negative operands whose sum reaches 8 or more, and 36 pairs of two negative operands whose sum falls below -8.
check.explanation: The asymmetry comes from -8 having no positive counterpart, so the negative side has eight values that can overflow downwards but only seven that cannot. Recomputed by enumerating all 256 ordered pairs in scripts/validate.py.

sources.note: read the opening of the lecture: flags are bits that are set or reset depending on the operation, a conditional instruction tests them to decide whether to branch or fall through, and conditional and unconditional branches are distinguished by whether a condition is tested.
